exposure: Placement of a central suction negative pressure wound therapy system
cohort: Ten patients from the Gynecology and Obstetrics Department at the General Hospital of Zapopan with infected and dehiscence surgical wounds (8 post-cesarean section, 1 post-hysterectomy, 1 with Fournier's gangrene) were included.
finding: The central suction negative pressure wound therapy technique is a cost-effective alternative for managing surgical wounds with favorable outcomes in low-resource settings.
